policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere תֹצְאֹתָ֖יו and ketiv תצאתו differ only in the plene vs defective writing of the same noun and suffix; ASV 'and the goings out thereof were at the sea' renders the plural noun with a possessive suffix either way, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit, so the English does not distinguish the readings. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
